newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CANOEING-CHAMPION OPTS NOT TO DEFEND BERG TITLE.
newsitem.headline: CANOEING-CHAMPION OPTS NOT TO DEFEND BERG TITLE.

text.p: Six-time Berg River Canoe marathon champion Robbie Herreveld will not be defending his title in the 1997 race.
The 25-year-old paddler told Reuters on Wednesday that he had opted to take a year off from the sport to concentrate on business and avoid the risk of "burn-out".
"I've had enough basically," he said. "If I go on the way I am at the moment I can see burn-out coming.
"I'm busy trying to establish my sports shop and I've been concentrating on (that). Hopefully I will come back hungry and motivated next year."
Herreveld has made the 215km race down the Berg River from Paarl to Port Owen his own since first entering as a 15-year-old.

He won six junior titles before graduating to the senior ranks where he promptly reeled off another half-dozen titles eclipsing Jean Hugo's previous record of five wins in the gruelling four-day event.
"I love the race, and I feel quite sad that I am not going to do it, but I feel it's all for the good," added Herreveld.
"There's a lot of training and a lot of pressure and I needed a break."
This year's race, in which there is 100,000 rand at stake, takes place from July 9-12.
